extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, supervisory examiners, OPQA staff, Technology Center directors, and patent quality/training personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for reviewing patent examiner work product and designing/delivering training to improve patent examination quality within the USPTO (OPQA/TC context). Covers review types, the Master Review Form, statutory compliance standards, quality metrics, and continuous improvement processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Examiner Training (PTA categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: New Examiner Training; Legal Practice & Procedure; Continuing Education Training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the primary training categories delivered via the Patent Training Academy (PTA) to develop examiner skills and legal knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Practice & Procedure Training components
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes Examiner Refresher Training, Master Class Program, Patent Quality Chats for Patent Examiners, Legal Lecture Series, Patent Law and Evidence Legal Course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is provided to both newly hired and experienced examiners; may be delivered corps-wide or to specific disciplines; refresher legal training can be lecture style, interactive computer-based training (CBT), workshops, or combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Education Training elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs such as the Patent Examiner Technical Training Program (PETTP), Site Experience Education (SEE) Program, Updated Automation Tools Training, Tuition Assistance Program (Non-Duty Hours Legal Studies and Technical Training), and Stakeholder Training on Examination Practice and Procedure (STEPP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to enhance technical and legal knowledge pertaining to examination of patent applications; may include non-duty hours tuition assistance and stakeholder-facing training.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPQA activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducts reviews of examiner work product; analyzes results and other quality data to report quality metrics and trends; assists Technology Centers (TCs) with quality improvement efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA functions as the office-level quality assurance organization supporting data-driven quality reporting and TC assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of OPQA Reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Random Reviews (OPQA randomly samples about 1% of Office actions), Ad Hoc Reviews (TCs or other organizations can request reviews of specific Office actions, e.g., pilot assessments), Case Study Reviews (in-depth assessments on particular issues, e.g., aspects of 35 U.S.C. § 101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Random reviews are used to derive metrics to TC level; ad hoc and case-study reviews support targeted assessments and pilots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master Review Form (MRF) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: MRF is used by RQAS and SPEs to record findings and captures information about statutory compliance, clarity, and other aspects such as the response to arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MRF is the primary instrument for recording review results that feed quality metrics and improvement efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRF design and question scope
rubrics_metrics.description: MRF is a modular designed smart-form with 20+ modules (e.g., Omitted/Made Rejections, Search, etc.) and a 330-question library covering correctness, clarity, best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers select relevant modules; the extensive question library structures determination of compliance, clarity, and best practices. (Full MRF available on USPTO site.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory Compliance Standard — allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For an allowed claim, the Office action must: not omit a statutorily compliant rejection, clearly identify the claim, and set forth that the claim is allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An allowance must affirmatively show that applicable rejections were considered and that the claim is properly identified and determined allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory Compliance Standard — rejected claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For a rejected claim, the Office action must: clearly identify the claim, identify the relevant statute, and set forth sufficient evidence to put a person skilled in the art on notice as to why the claim is unpatentable to provide applicant with a fair opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejections must include clear claim identification, statutory basis, and adequate reasoning/evidence so the applicant can meaningfully respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing Random Reviews — disposition flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the review, RQAS flags the action as Non-compliant, Needs attention, or Pass through.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality Lead checks findings of non-compliance before returning case to the Technology Center; TCs may rebut; appeals may proceed to OPQA Director and Deputy Commissioner for Patent Quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: TC Reviews vs OPQA Reviews — standards and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: TC Reviews follow Performance Appraisal Plan (PAP) standards (depends on GS level) and may be conducted before or after mailing; OPQA Reviews focus on Statutory Compliance and are conducted after mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes local performance-oriented reviews (which can be pre-mailing) from office-wide statutory compliance reviews (post-mailing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Metrics — product indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture both correctness and clarity of examiners’ final work product using the MRF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product indicators derive from MRF findings and inform measures of legal correctness and clarity in Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Metrics — process indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Track the efficiency and consistency of processes (for example, to identify 'churning' from re-work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process indicators monitor workflow health and re-work patterns to guide process improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Metrics — perception indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Surveys to internally and externally poll perceptions of patent quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perception metrics supplement product/process measures with stakeholder viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: FY18 Statutory Compliance Targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Target statutory compliance rates for FY18: 35 U.S.C. §101 >97%, §112 >93%, §102 >95%, §103 >93% (confidence level +/-1.5%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric targets used for performance monitoring and assessing quality initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance methods for TCs with quality improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools include Sig Panels, Appeal Conferences, Delivering Training, Mentoring, and other assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA and quality leads deploy these interventions to address identified weaknesses and improve TC performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: TC 2800 Continuous Quality Improvement process
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements include Agency Level vs TC Level Training, Identify Areas of Need (data-driven), Assess Strengths and Weaknesses (root causes) via case reviews and discussions with Supervisors, Trainers and Reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes data-driven needs identification and root-cause analysis before training development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous Quality Improvement cycle for training
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop appropriate training (determine format), deliver training, assess effectiveness of training (determine measures and SMART goals), and revise materials and delivery methods as appropriate (after action review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should include quantitative and qualitative measures and result in iterative improvement of training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data gathering sources for quality assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes Efficiency Report (Pendency), Transactional Quality Index Report (QIR), Timeliness Reports (SPE Dashboard), big data sources, and OPQA statistical data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical, current, and transactional data to inform needs assessments and monitor outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive review sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive reviews include Supervisory Reviews, OPQA Reviews, Conferences, Signatory Review, Appeal, and Pilot Program reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple review inputs provide broader evidence about examiner performance and systemic issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess training needs and prioritize goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify types of errors or weaknesses, identify root causes, prioritize TC training goals considering Office Strategic Goals and Executive Goals, and identify a team to develop and deliver training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritization should align TC training with broader office objectives and target root causes rather than symptoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop training — reuse and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Look to previously developed training resources and modify if necessary; developing new materials requires approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage existing content where possible; obtain required approvals for new training materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training delivery formats and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Formats include large or small lectures, small group lectures with Q&A, one-on-one or very small groups, workshops, peer trainings, computer-based trainings, email/chat Q&A, combinations; duration may be once, few, or regular sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose delivery format and cadence appropriate to the training goals and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess effectiveness of training — measures and SMART goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a measure and a SMART goal; measures may be OPQA statistics, QIR statistics, case reviews before and after, quizzes/questionnaires; goals may include qualitative and quantitative measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound goals to evaluate training impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: After Action Reviews for training
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions include: What went well, what worked? What aspects were less effective or failed? What will be kept or changed in the next training iteration?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured after-action review to capture lessons and inform revisions.
